findings.claim: The generator now puts `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` on its half of the user's `partial class` resolver (ResolverTemplate and CompositeResolverTemplate). The attribute has AllowMultiple = false. A user who already marks their `[GeneratedMessagePackResolver] partial class X` with `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` (the obvious manual workaround before this change) now gets CS0579 'Duplicate ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute', so existing projects stop compiling.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageEdgeCaseTests.UserResolverAlreadyExcludedFromCoverage_CompilesWithoutErrors. It runs MessagePackGenerator on a user partial resolver that already carries [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] and asserts the output compilation has no errors. On head it reports CS0579; on base it compiles.

findings.claim: The guard `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK` is wider than it needs to be. `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute` exists in netstandard2.0 and in every .NET Framework version MessagePack supports (4.0+), and it applies to classes there. Yet the attribute is dropped for every library targeting netstandard2.0 or net4x, which is a large share of consumers. So the requirement 'all generated code is decorated' is not met on those targets. Conditional emission was only justified where the attribute does not exist.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageEdgeCaseTests.FormattersExcludedFromCoverage_WhenNetStandard20SymbolDefined. It compiles with preprocessor symbol NETSTANDARD2_0 against references that contain the attribute, then asserts every generated IMessagePackFormatter<T> implementation carries ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute. On head the attribute is stripped.
